full_judgment: 2. Plaintiff's case, in short, is that the suit land appertaining to nishkar jama recorded in khatian No.65 of mouza Monoharpur originally belonged to one Kefattullah Sonar. He died leaving two wives Abijan and Tenjore Bibi, four sons Kasim, Nasir, Kasimuddin and Kinjaruddin and five daughters—Abijan, Shabijan, Mobijan Gondli Bibi and Dhali Bibi. Nasir died leaving mother Abijan and full brother Kasir and then Kasir died leaving his mother Abijan two step brothers Kasim and Kinjor and five step sisters. Kasim died leaving son defendant No.1 Abdul Gani, and widow defendant No. 2 Karimonnessa and also a daughter, Kulsum. Sabijan died leaving mother, Tanjor, husband Sayek Mamud, full brother Kinjor and two full sisters—Gondli and Mobijan and then Mobijan died leaving a son Mahabbat (Plff. 4), daughter Bonbashi and mother Tanjor. Then Tanjor died leaving a son Kinjor (Pltff. l) and a daughter Gondli. Kulsum died leaving husband Mortaza Hossain, mother Karimonnessa (defdt. No. 2) brother Abdul Gani (defdt.1). Kefaitulla's predeceased widow Abijan Bibi orally gifted away her share to plaintiff No.1 Kinjoruddin in 1330 B.S. The plaintiff had also purchased the share of Kulsom and Sayek Mamud by two separate kabalas. Thus the plaintiffs got 12 annas and 2-208/1053 pies share by inheritance and purchase. The plaintiffs have been possessing 56 decimals of land from the western portion of the suit land as their share by partition for the last 12 years, and the defendant have been possessing eastern 16 or 17 decimals of land. The defendants, however, claimed the entire land and threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs from their share. Hence this suit.
